page: Google Cloud Platform e2-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, meaning all storage must be attached over the network.

Benchmark results place the e2-standard-4 in the lower performance tiers. In stress-ng CPU testing, both single-core and multi-core performance fall within the bottom 25 percent. Similarly, Geekbench scores are low, with single-core and multi-core results in the bottom 10 percent, alongside poor software compilation and image processing speeds. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 24.13 GB/sec for large block read-only operations. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in LLM text generation for small 135M models, achieving 104.71 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the e2-standard-4 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio without demanding high-performance compute. The trade-off is lower raw processing power and memory throughput. This profile makes the instance suitable for lightweight web serving, basic database operations, and small-scale development or testing environments that do not require intensive CPU or disk I/O.
